title: Cravings, Burdens, and Shared Leadership
overview: In the desert the people complain and long for the food of Egypt, Moses breaks down under the weight of leading them, and God answers by sharing the load with seventy elders and sending meat that ends in a plague.

parts.label: Complaining and fire (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The people grumble about the hardships of the road, and fire from the LORD burns the edge of the camp until Moses prays and it dies down. The place is named Taberah, meaning "burning," so the name keeps the memory alive.

parts.label: Longing for Egypt's food (vv. 4-9)
parts.note: A mixed group traveling with Israel, probably non-Israelites who left Egypt with them, starts craving meat, and soon everyone is weeping for Egypt's fish and vegetables, as if slavery had been a feast. The careful description of manna, which came down with the dew at night, shows it was good food that could be ground, boiled or baked.

parts.label: Moses reaches his limit (vv. 10-15)
parts.note: Moses protests that he never gave birth to this people, so why must he carry them like a nurse carrying a baby? Overwhelmed, he asks God to end his life rather than leave him alone with the load, and the text records this raw protest without smoothing it over.

parts.label: Helpers and meat promised (vv. 16-23)
parts.note: God promises to share the Spirit resting on Moses with seventy elders so they can help carry the people, and to send meat for a whole month until they are sick of it, because they have rejected the LORD who is with them. When Moses doubts there could be that much food, God asks whether his power has limits and tells him to watch.

parts.label: The Spirit on the elders (vv. 24-30)
parts.note: The seventy prophesy once at the tent, and two listed elders, Eldad and Medad, prophesy back in the camp, though what this looked like is unclear and interpreters differ on whether it was a passing sign or a lasting gift for leading. When Joshua urges Moses to stop the two, Moses wishes all the LORD's people had the Spirit, a wish Christians read as fulfilled when the Spirit later came on believers broadly.

parts.label: Quail and the graves (vv. 31-35)
parts.note: A wind from the LORD drives in huge numbers of quail, small migrating birds, and people gather them for two days; it is unclear whether "two cubits," about three feet, means the birds lay piled up or flew that low. While the people are still eating, a severe plague strikes, and the place is named Kibroth Hattaavah, "graves of craving"; the text gives the LORD's anger as the cause and explains no further.

think: Why might people remember a hard past as better than it really was when the present feels uncertain?
